original_question: Heath-Brown proved a Weyl-strength twelfth-moment bound for the Riemann zeta function, Jutila proved an analogous sixth-moment result in the t-aspect for L(1/2 + it, f) with f a Hecke-Maass cusp form, and complementary twelfth-moment results are known for Dirichlet L-functions in the level aspect. Prove the analogous Weyl-strength bound for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f tensor chi).
target_in_paper: Problem (12) in the section "Moments of the Riemann zeta function": the paper asks, after recalling Heath-Brown’s Weyl-strength twelfth moment for ζ(s), Jutila’s t-aspect sixth moment for L(1/2+it,f), and recent level-aspect twelfth moments for Dirichlet L-functions, whether one can prove analogous bounds for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f ⊗ χ).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual formulation. It names exactly the same comparison results in the same order—Heath-Brown for the zeta twelfth moment, Jutila for the t-aspect sixth moment of L(1/2+it,f), and recent level-aspect twelfth-moment work for Dirichlet L-functions—and it asks for the same target problem: a Weyl-strength sixth-moment bound for L(1/2, f ⊗ χ).
missing_details: The paper treats this as a level/Dirichlet-character aspect problem: χ should be understood as varying with conductor (or modulus) growing, not as a t-aspect, weight-aspect, or spectral-aspect problem.
The question is for a fixed Hecke–Maass cusp form f; the draft mentions the type of f but does not explicitly say that f is fixed while χ varies.

The paper itself does not specify the exact normalization of the χ-family (primitive versus all characters, fixed modulus q versus conductor window up to Q), so a stand-alone version should state only the level-aspect variation and avoid overcommitting to a convention not given in the paper.
Likewise, the paper does not specify extra hypotheses on f such as level 1, nebentypus, or holomorphic versus Maass beyond saying that f is a Hecke–Maass cusp form, so those should not be inserted.

The phrase "analogous Weyl-strength bound" is implicit in the paper through the cited analogies; a stand-alone formulation should make clear that the desired benchmark is the level-aspect analogue of Heath-Brown’s and Jutila’s moment bounds, not a broader asymptotic formula or a different family.
refined_question: Let f be a fixed Hecke–Maass cusp form. As Dirichlet characters χ vary with conductor tending to infinity, prove a Weyl-strength upper bound for the sixth moment of the central twists L(1/2, f ⊗ χ), in direct analogy with Heath-Brown’s bound ∫_0^T |ζ(1/2+it)|^12 dt ≪_ε T^(2+ε), Jutila’s t-aspect sixth-moment bound for L(1/2+it,f), and the recent level-aspect twelfth-moment bounds for Dirichlet L-functions.
justification: This is Problem (12), not a neighboring problem. The paper’s official formulation on page 7 reproduces the same three comparison results that appear in your draft and then asks, almost verbatim, whether one can prove analogous bounds for the sixth moment of L(1/2, f ⊗ χ). There is no sharper theorem, conjecture, or equivalent reformulation elsewhere in the paper for this item, so the nearest paper-faithful target is exactly Problem (12). The rewrite therefore keeps the scope narrow: fixed Hecke–Maass cusp form f, χ varying in the level aspect, and a Weyl-strength sixth-moment bound for the twisted central values. It deliberately avoids adding paper-unsupported choices such as level 1 for f or a primitive/all-character averaging convention, since Problem (12) does not specify them, whereas other problems in the list explicitly state such restrictions when intended.
